To divide an $80\text{ mm}$ long straight line segment $AB$ in the ratio $2:3:4$:

1. Draw a given straight line $AB = 80\text{ mm}$ horizontally.
2. From end point $A$, draw an inclined line $AC$ at an acute angle (approx. $30^\circ$ to $45^\circ$) to $AB$.
3. Find the sum of the ratio parts: $2 + 3 + 4 = 9$.
4. Using a compass, mark $9$ equal divisions of arbitrary convenient length consecutively along the line $AC$ ($1, 2, 3, \dots, 9$).
5. Join the 9th division point to $B$.
6. Draw parallel lines through the 2nd and 5th division points on $AC$ to intersect line $AB$ at points $D$ and $E$.
7. The line $AB$ is now divided into segments $AD$, $DE$, and $EB$ in the exact ratio of $2:3:4$.
proTip: Keep the compass arc length small enough so that all 9 divisions easily fit on the inclined construction line.
